The pool drained quickly, causing QueuePool timeouts in the API pods, and the edge gateway started returning 504 errors.","likely_cause":"Exhaustion of the catalog‑API’s limited SQLAlchemy connection pool after the May 2025 update","confidence":"medium","claims":[{"text":"The deployment used async workers with a SQLAlchemy pool limited to 10 connections plus 5 overflow (max 30 sessions).","evidence_ids":["RB-028#1"],"quote":"SQLAlchemy pool allows 10 connections plus 5 overflow, so at most 30 sessions"},{"text":"The limited pool drained quickly, leading to QueuePool timeouts logged by catalog‑API pods.","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#1"],"quote":"pods hold only 30 between them, so the pool drained"},{"text":"The edge gateway began returning 504 errors as a symptom of the slowdown.","evidence_ids":["INC-0042#0"],"quote":"edge-gateway began answering 504"}],"next_checks":["Check release notes for May 2025 to see if the SQLAlchemy pool size or async worker count was changed","Review connection‑pool metrics during the incident window to confirm exhaustion","Examine cache‑miss rates to see if increased load contributed","Validate that the pool configuration was not overridden by a later change"]}
